events.title: Establishment of École de Médecine de Pondichéry (Precursor to JIPMER)
events.summary: French India established the École de Médecine de Pondichéry to train medical practitioners, creating one of the earliest institutions of tropical medicine in Asia. Following Puducherry's transfer to India, it evolved into the Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER).
events.sourceTitle: Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research - Wikipedia

events.title: Clara Swain Hospital Treats First In-Patients in Bareilly
events.summary: Dr. Clara Swain treated the first in-patients at the newly completed Clara Swain Hospital in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh. It became the first hospital dedicated specifically to women in India.

events.title: DCGI Approves Covaxin and Covishield for Emergency Use
events.summary: India's national regulatory authority, the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) under CDSCO, granted restricted emergency use approval to Bharat Biotech's indigenous Covaxin and Serum Institute of India's Covishield. This cleared the path for India's nationwide COVID-19 immunization campaign.
events.sourceTitle: Balancing Healthcare and Economy Amidst the COVID-19 Pandemic - PMC

events.title: Passing of Dr. P. K. Sethi, Co-Inventor of the Jaipur Foot
events.summary: Indian orthopaedic surgeon Pramod Karan Sethi passed away in Jaipur at age 80. Alongside craftsman Ram Chandra Sharma, he co-invented the low-cost, flexible Jaipur Foot prosthetic in 1969, restoring mobility to hundreds of thousands of amputees worldwide.

events.title: Birth of Nobel Laureate Har Gobind Khorana
events.summary: Biochemist Har Gobind Khorana was born in Raipur, British India. He shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Marshall Nirenberg and Robert Holley for demonstrating how nucleotide sequences in nucleic acids encode protein synthesis.
events.sourceTitle: Har Gobind Khorana | Biography, Nobel Prize, & Facts - Britannica

events.title: Pandit Madhusudan Gupta Performs First Modern Human Dissection in India
events.summary: Ayurvedic scholar and medical educator Pandit Madhusudan Gupta, assisted by four students under Professor Henry Goodeve's supervision, performed the first human cadaver dissection in modern India at Calcutta Medical College. The act broke entrenched social taboos and established practical anatomy in Indian medical education.
events.sourceTitle: A Trailblazer in Anatomy: Madhusudan Gupta and the Historic First Dissection - PMC

events.title: Waldemar Haffkine Tests First Plague Vaccine on Himself in Bombay
events.summary: During the bubonic plague epidemic in Bombay (Mumbai), bacteriologist Waldemar Haffkine inoculated himself to prove the safety of his newly developed anti-plague vaccine. Subsequent controlled trials at Byculla jail confirmed its protective efficacy, leading to millions of inoculations across India.

events.title: Birth of Dr. Yellapragada Subbarow
events.summary: Biochemist Yellapragada Subbarow was born in Bhimavaram, Andhra Pradesh. His landmark discoveries included elucidating the role of ATP as cellular energy, synthesizing folic acid, and developing methotrexate, tetracycline antibiotics, and diethylcarbamazine (Hetrazan).
events.sourceTitle: Yellapragada Subbarow: A Pioneer in Biomedical Research - PMC

events.title: India's Last Reported Case of Wild Poliovirus
events.summary: Two-year-old Rukhsar Khatoon in Howrah, West Bengal, was recorded as India's final case of wild poliovirus infection. Sustained Pulse Polio immunization and surveillance thereafter paved the way for India's polio-free certification in 2014.
events.sourceTitle: World Immunization Day 2024 - Press Information Bureau

events.title: India's First Successful Bilateral Hand Transplant
events.summary: A surgical team led by Dr. Subramaniam Iyer at Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences in Kochi, Kerala, performed India's first successful bilateral hand transplant. The recipient regained functional use of both transplanted limbs after intensive rehabilitation.
events.sourceTitle: A Helping Hand - The New Indian Express

events.title: Birth of Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay, Indian IVF Pioneer
events.summary: Physician and scientist Subhash Mukhopadhyay was born in Hazaribagh, British India. In 1978, he created India's first—and the world's second—test-tube baby using in vitro fertilization and cryopreservation.

events.title: Launch of India's Nationwide COVID-19 Vaccination Drive
events.summary: India launched the world's largest COVID-19 vaccination campaign, initially prioritizing healthcare and frontline workers using Covishield and Covaxin tracked via the Co-WIN digital platform.
events.sourceTitle: PM Launches pan India rollout of COVID-19 vaccination drive - PIB

events.title: Birth of Sir Leonard Rogers, Tropical Medicine Pioneer
events.summary: Indian Medical Service officer Sir Leonard Rogers was born. As professor of pathology at Calcutta Medical College, he pioneered treatments for cholera and leprosy and founded the Calcutta School of Tropical Medicine.

events.title: Passing of Dr. V. Shanta, Champion of Affordable Cancer Care
events.summary: Renowned Indian oncologist and longtime Chairperson of the Adyar Cancer Institute in Chennai, Dr. Viswanathan Shanta, passed away at age 93. She was honoured with the Ramon Magsaysay Award and the Padma Vibhushan for making quality cancer care accessible to the poor.

events.title: Dr. Clara Swain Arrives in Bareilly as First Missionary Woman Physician
events.summary: American physician Dr. Clara Swain arrived in Bareilly, India, becoming the first fully accredited female doctor sent by a missionary society to India. She soon began training local Indian women in clinical medicine and established India's first hospital for women.

events.title: Formation of the Indian Army Medical Corps (AMC)
events.summary: Upon India becoming a republic, the Indian Army Medical Corps (IAMC)—formed in 1943 by amalgamating the Indian Medical Service, Indian Medical Department, and Indian Hospital & Nursing Corps—was officially re-designated as the Army Medical Corps (AMC).

events.title: Establishment of Calcutta Medical College
events.summary: Governor-General Lord William Bentinck established the Calcutta Medical College (now Medical College & Hospital, Kolkata) to provide structured education in modern Western medicine. It stands as one of the oldest modern medical colleges in Asia.

events.title: First Confirmed Case of COVID-19 in India
events.summary: India reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 in Kerala, marking the onset of the country's pandemic surveillance, testing, and public health response.
events.sourceTitle: COVID-19: in the direction of monitoring the pandemic in India - PMC

events.title: National Strategic Plan for Leprosy (2023–27) and Nikusth 2.0 Launched
events.summary: Observed annually in India on January 30 as National Anti-Leprosy Day (commemorating Mahatma Gandhi's death anniversary), the 2023 observance saw the release of the National Strategic Plan & Roadmap for Leprosy (2023–27) and the Nikusth 2.0 digital case-management portal under NLEP.
events.sourceTitle: Challenges of sustaining leprosy elimination in India - IJFCM

events.title: Birth of Dr. Sambhu Nath De, Discoverer of Cholera Toxin
events.summary: Indian medical scientist and pathologist Sambhu Nath De was born in Garibati, Bengal. Using ligated rabbit ileal loops, he discovered the cholera enterotoxin in 1959, transforming global understanding of cholera pathogenesis and secretory diarrhea.

events.title: Establishment of Madras Medical College
events.summary: Madras Medical College (MMC) was founded in Chennai, attached to the Government General Hospital. Alongside Calcutta Medical College, it is one of the oldest modern medical institutions in India.

events.title: Robert Koch Reports Discovery of the Cholera Bacillus from Calcutta
events.summary: Working in Calcutta (Kolkata), German microbiologist Robert Koch reported his reasoned conviction on the identification of the comma-shaped cholera bacillus (Vibrio cholerae) as the causative agent of cholera.
events.sourceTitle: Robert Koch and the cholera vibrio: a centenary - The BMJ

events.title: India's First Successful Kidney Transplant at CMC Vellore
events.summary: Dr. A. Mohan Rao and Dr. K. V. Johny performed India's first successful living-donor kidney transplant at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, ushering in the era of organ transplantation in India.
events.sourceTitle: It is 50 years since Vellore CMC performed the country's first kidney transplant - The Hindu

events.title: Passing of Sir Upendranath Brahmachari
events.summary: Indian physician and scientist Sir Upendranath Brahmachari died in Kolkata at age 72. He synthesized Urea Stibamine in 1922, an organic antimonial compound that dramatically reduced mortality from kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) across India.

events.title: Passing of Dr. E. K. Janaki Ammal
events.summary: Pioneering Indian botanist and cytogeneticist Edavalath Kakkat Janaki Ammal passed away in Chennai. Her cytogenetic research on medicinal and crop plants advanced botanical science and phytogeography in India.

events.title: Launch of National Deworming Day (NDD)
events.summary: India's Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched National Deworming Day to combat soil-transmitted helminth infections among children and adolescents aged 1–19 years using albendazole, growing into the world's largest single-day public health deworming program.

events.title: India Certified Free of Guinea Worm Disease
events.summary: At its February 2000 meeting, the International Commission for the Certification of Dracunculiasis Eradication (ICCDE) reviewed the International Certification Team's report on India, leading to WHO certifying India as free of Guinea worm disease following zero reported cases since 1996.
events.sourceTitle: Guinea Worm Eradication Programme (GWEP) - NCDC | MoHFW

events.title: Inauguration of Lady Hardinge Medical College, New Delhi
events.summary: Lady Hardinge Medical College (LHMC), one of India's earliest and premier medical colleges dedicated to women's medical education, was formally inaugurated in New Delhi by Lord Hardinge.

events.title: Inauguration of the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow
events.summary: Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru formally inaugurated the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow as one of post-independence India's first CSIR national laboratories dedicated to biomedical and pharmaceutical research.

events.title: AIIMS Bill Introduced in Lok Sabha by Rajkumari Amrit Kaur
events.summary: Union Health Minister Rajkumari Amrit Kaur introduced the bill in the Lok Sabha that became the All India Institute of Medical Sciences Act, 1956, establishing AIIMS New Delhi as an autonomous institute of national importance for medical education and research.
events.sourceTitle: All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Delhi - Wikipedia

events.title: Establishment of the Calcutta School of Tropical Medicine
events.summary: Founded by Sir Leonard Rogers of the Indian Medical Service, the Calcutta School of Tropical Medicine (CSTM) was established in Kolkata as a dedicated postgraduate research institute for tropical diseases.
events.sourceTitle: Calcutta School of Tropical Medicine - Wikipedia

events.title: Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Scheme First Implemented
events.summary: Administered by the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) under the ESI Act of 1948, India's social health insurance scheme for workers was first put into effect in Kanpur and Delhi.

events.title: Passing of Dr. Anandi Gopal Joshi
events.summary: Dr. Anandi Gopal Joshi, the first Indian woman to earn a degree in Western medicine, succumbed to tuberculosis in Pune at age 21, shortly after being appointed physician-in-charge of the female ward at Albert Edward Hospital in Kolhapur.

events.title: Commissioning of Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai
events.summary: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust commissioned Tata Memorial Hospital (TMH) in Parel, Mumbai, which grew into India's oldest and largest comprehensive cancer treatment and research center.

events.title: Release of Indigenous CSIR-CDRI Drugs and Leishmaniasis Diagnostic Kit
events.summary: Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao released new drugs developed by CSIR-CDRI (BESEB and Chandonium iodide) along with a diagnostic kit for leishmaniasis and new drug technologies to the nation.

events.title: Dr. Clara Swain Begins Formal Medical Training for Indian Women in Bareilly
events.summary: Dr. Clara Swain started instructing 14 native Indian women in anatomy, physiology, and materia medica in Bareilly, resulting in 13 graduates receiving practice certificates in 1873.

events.title: Passing of Dr. R. Marthanda Varma, Founder Director of NIMHANS
events.summary: Pioneering Indian neurosurgeon R. Marthanda Varma, the founder director of the National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS) in Bengaluru, passed away at age 92.

events.title: Dr. Anandi Gopal Joshi Graduates with an M.D. in the United States
events.summary: At age 21, Anandi Gopal Joshi graduated with a medical degree from the Woman's Medical College of Pennsylvania with a thesis on 'Obstetrics among the Aryan Hindus,' becoming the first Indian woman certified in Western medicine.

events.title: Birth of Dr. V. Shanta, Pioneering Indian Oncologist
events.summary: Dr. Viswanathan Shanta was born in Mylapore, Chennai. She dedicated over six decades to the Adyar Cancer Institute, transforming it into a premier center for free and subsidized cancer care.

events.title: India Confirms Its First COVID-19 Fatality
events.summary: Health authorities in Karnataka and the Union Health Ministry confirmed India's first COVID-19 death involving a 76-year-old man from Kalaburagi who had recently returned from Saudi Arabia.
events.sourceTitle: India's first COVID-19 death confirmed in Karnataka - The Hindu

events.title: Birth of Waldemar Haffkine, Cholera and Plague Vaccine Pioneer
events.summary: Bacteriologist Waldemar Mordecai Wolff Haffkine was born in Odessa. Working extensively in India from 1893 onward, he developed and deployed the first effective vaccines against cholera and bubonic plague.

events.title: First Dose of Oral Polio Vaccine Administered Under Pulse Polio
events.summary: India administered its first dose of the Oral Polio Vaccine under the Pulse Polio Immunisation Programme, a date now commemorated annually across the country as National Vaccination Day.

events.title: India Expands COVID-19 Vaccination to Ages 12–14 with Corbevax
events.summary: India launched COVID-19 immunization for children aged 12–14 years using the Hyderabad-based Biological E's indigenous Corbevax vaccine, alongside precautionary doses for all citizens aged 60 and above.
events.sourceTitle: India's efforts to achieve 1.5 billion COVID-19 vaccinations - PMC

events.title: Foundation Stone Laid for Lady Hardinge Medical College
events.summary: Lady Hardinge laid the foundation stone of Lady Hardinge Medical College in New Delhi, establishing a dedicated institution to train women physicians in India.

events.title: Passing of Dr. Biresh Chandra Guha, Father of Modern Biochemistry in India
events.summary: Indian biochemist Biresh Chandra Guha died at age 57. He established biochemistry as an independent academic discipline in India and made key contributions to vitamin, nutrition, and food science research, including during the 1943 Bengal famine.

events.title: First Administration of Ether Anaesthesia in India
events.summary: Just five months after William Morton's Boston demonstration, ether anaesthesia was administered for the first time in India at Medical College Hospital, Calcutta, under the supervision of Dr. R. O'Shaughnessy.
events.sourceTitle: Ether day: an intriguing history - PMC

events.title: Birth of Dame Edith Mary Brown, Founder of CMC Ludhiana
events.summary: Medical missionary Dame Edith Mary Brown was born. In 1894, she founded the North India School of Medicine for Christian Women in Ludhiana—now Christian Medical College (CMC), Ludhiana—Asia's first medical school for women.
events.sourceTitle: CMC's history | Friends of Ludhiana Australia

events.title: India Imposes Nationwide 21-Day COVID-19 Lockdown
events.summary: To curb local and community transmission of SARS-CoV-2, the Government of India implemented a complete nationwide 21-day lockdown, one of the largest pandemic containment measures in history.
events.sourceTitle: Impact of lockdown to control over Novel Coronavirus and COVID-19 in India - PMC

events.title: WHO Officially Certifies India as Polio-Free
events.summary: The World Health Organization officially certified India, along with ten other countries in the WHO South-East Asia Region, as polio-free—marking a historic triumph of the Universal Immunization Programme and Pulse Polio campaign.
events.sourceTitle: World Immunization Day 2024 - Press Information Bureau

events.title: Birth of Dr. Anandi Gopal Joshi
events.summary: Anandi Gopal Joshi (born Yamuna Joshi) was born in Kalyan, Maharashtra. Overcoming severe societal barriers, she became the first Indian woman to obtain a degree in Western medicine in 1886.

events.title: Birth of Dr. T. S. Kanaka, Asia's First Female Neurosurgeon
events.summary: Thanjavur Santhanakrishna Kanaka was born in Chennai. She became Asia's first female neurosurgeon and pioneered stereotactic neurosurgery and chronic electrode implantation in India.

events.title: Birth of Nobel Laureate Venkatraman Ramakrishnan
events.summary: Structural biologist Sir Venkatraman Ramakrishnan was born in Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu. He won the 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for mapping the atomic structure of the ribosome, advancing understanding of how antibiotics bind to bacterial ribosomes.
events.sourceTitle: Venki Ramakrishnan, Ph.D. | Academy of Achievement

events.title: Sanction of the All India Institute of Mental Health (NIMHANS)
events.summary: Following recommendations from the Mudaliar and Bhore Committees, the Government of India sanctioned the establishment of the All India Institute of Mental Health in Bengaluru. It was later amalgamated with the Mysore Mental Hospital in 1974 to form NIMHANS.

events.title: Launch of Aarogya Setu COVID-19 App
events.summary: The Government of India launched Aarogya Setu, a national digital contact-tracing and COVID-19 risk-assessment application developed in 11 languages. It amassed 50 million downloads within two weeks and later integrated with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission.
events.sourceTitle: lessons learned from national LMIC COVID applications - PMC - NIH

events.title: Launch of India's First Indigenous CAR-T Cell Therapy (NexCAR19)
events.summary: President Droupadi Murmu formally launched NexCAR19 (actalycabtagene autoleucel), India's first home-grown gene therapy for B-cell lymphomas and leukaemia. Developed by IIT Bombay, Tata Memorial Centre, and ImmunoACT, it became the world's most affordable CAR-T therapy.
events.sourceTitle: India's First Home-Grown Gene Therapy - Press Information Bureau

events.title: Birth of Pulmonologist Dr. Randeep Guleria
events.summary: Padma Shri pulmonologist and former AIIMS New Delhi Director Dr. Randeep Guleria was born in Himachal Pradesh. He is credited with establishing India's first dedicated centre for pulmonary medicine and sleep disorders at AIIMS.

events.title: Pasteur Institute of Southern India Begins Operations in Coonoor
events.summary: The Pasteur Institute of Southern India (now the Pasteur Institute of India) started functioning in Coonoor, Tamil Nadu. It became a pioneering national hub for producing anti-rabies, influenza, trivalent oral polio, and DPT vaccines.

events.title: Passing of Biophysicist G. N. Ramachandran
events.summary: Gopalasamudram Narayanan Ramachandran, FRS, passed away in Chennai at age 78. He created the Ramachandran plot for protein and peptide conformations and was the first to propose a triple-helical structure for collagen.

events.title: Enactment of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017
events.summary: India's Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 received presidential assent, replacing the Mental Health Act of 1987. It established a rights-based legal framework guaranteeing access to mental healthcare, advance directives, and the decriminalization of attempted suicide.

events.title: Passing of Cancer Researcher Dr. Kamal Ranadive
events.summary: Padma Bhushan biomedical researcher Kamal Ranadive passed away at age 83. She established India's first tissue culture research laboratory at the Indian Cancer Research Centre in Mumbai and pioneered studies on links between viruses and cancer.

events.title: India Declares National Safe Motherhood Day
events.summary: The Government of India declared April 11, Kasturba Gandhi's birth anniversary, as National Safe Motherhood Day following an initiative by the White Ribbon Alliance India. India became the first country in the world to officially designate a national day for safe motherhood.
events.sourceTitle: National Safe Motherhood day 2020: Importance, history, quotes and more - India Today

events.title: Launch of National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and Janani Suraksha Yojana
events.summary: The Government of India launched the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) alongside the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) cash-incentive safe motherhood scheme. Together, they transformed rural primary healthcare infrastructure and dramatically increased institutional deliveries.
events.sourceTitle: National Rural Health Mission: Turning into Reality - PMC

events.title: Dr. Viswanathan Shanta Joins Adyar Cancer Institute
events.summary: Oncologist Dr. Viswanathan Shanta joined the Cancer Institute (WIA) in Adyar, Chennai as an honorary staff member when it was a 12-bed cottage hospital. Over the next six decades, she transformed it into a globally recognized oncology center and established India's first pediatric oncology institute.
events.sourceTitle: Redefining Cancer Care in India: Dr. Viswanathan Shanta's Lasting Legacy - PMC

events.title: Inauguration of First Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centre
events.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated India's first Health and Wellness Centre (HWC) under the Ayushman Bharat programme at Jangla village in Bijapur district, Chhattisgarh. The initiative aimed to upgrade 150,000 primary healthcare centres across the country.
events.sourceTitle: Narendra Modi opens health centre under Ayushman Bharat - The Hindu

events.title: First Postgraduate Medical Classes Begin at PGIMER Chandigarh
events.summary: Classes for the inaugural batch of postgraduate medical students commenced at the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER) in Chandigarh, which later became an Institute of National Importance.
events.sourceTitle: At 50, PGI set to walk down memory lane of golden past - The Indian Express

events.title: Passing of Cholera Toxin Discoverer Dr. Sambhu Nath De
events.summary: Indian medical scientist Dr. Sambhu Nath De passed away in Kolkata at age 70. His 1959 discovery of the cholera enterotoxin and development of the ligated rabbit ileal loop model revolutionized cholera pathophysiology and paved the way for oral rehydration therapy.

events.title: Passing of IVF Pioneer Dr. Baidyanath Chakrabarty
events.summary: Reproductive medicine pioneer Dr. Baidyanath Chakrabarty passed away in Kolkata. A collaborator of Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay, he founded the Institute of Reproductive Medicine in Salt Lake and performed over 4,000 IVF procedures during a seven-decade career.

events.title: India Certified Free of Smallpox
events.summary: The International Commission for the Assessment of Eradication of Smallpox officially declared India free of smallpox following the intensified Operation Smallpox Zero campaign.
events.sourceTitle: A Review of the Final Phases of the Smallpox Eradication Program in India - PMC

events.title: Official Opening of Pasteur Institute of Southern India, Coonoor
events.summary: Sir Arthur Lawley, Governor of Madras, officially opened the Pasteur Institute of Southern India at Coonoor. The institute was funded in part by a philanthropic grant to Viceroy Lord Curzon to expand anti-rabies vaccine access in India.

events.title: Birth of Medical Education Pioneer Dr. T. M. A. Pai
events.summary: Physician, banker, and educationist Dr. Tonse Madhava Ananth Pai was born in Kallianpur, Udupi. He founded Kasturba Medical College in Manipal in 1953, establishing India's first private, self-financing MBBS medical college.

events.title: Establishment of Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC), Pune
events.summary: Armed Forces Medical College was established in Pune on the recommendation of the B. C. Roy Committee by amalgamating Indian Army Medical Corps units into a postgraduate teaching institution.

events.title: India Expands COVID-19 Vaccination to All Adults (18+)
events.summary: India opened Phase 3 of its national COVID-19 vaccination drive to all eligible adults aged 18 and above, alongside the arrival of the first consignment of Sputnik V vaccines.

events.title: Birth of Clinical Scientist Dr. Soumya Swaminathan
events.summary: Pediatrician and tuberculosis/HIV researcher Dr. Soumya Swaminathan was born in Chennai. She served as Director General of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and later became the Chief Scientist of the World Health Organization.

events.title: Establishment of Central Research Institute (CRI), Kasauli
events.summary: The Central Research Institute was established in Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh as a premier national centre for medical research, antisera, and vaccine manufacturing including DTP and tetanus toxoid.

events.title: WHO Declares India Free of Yaws
events.summary: Based on the International Verification Team's recommendations, the WHO Director-General formally declared India free of yaws in Geneva, making India the first country in the world to achieve WHO-certified yaws elimination.

events.title: Passing of Kala-azar Pioneer Dr. Mohan Mishra
events.summary: Padma Shri physician Dr. Mohan Mishra passed away at age 83. He was renowned for his pioneering clinical work demonstrating the efficacy of Amphotericin B in treating visceral leishmaniasis (Kala-azar) in India.

events.title: Birth of Cardiac Surgeon Dr. Devi Shetty
events.summary: Padma Bhushan cardiac surgeon Dr. Devi Prasad Shetty was born in Kinnigoli, Karnataka. Founder of Narayana Health, he has performed over 15,000 heart operations and pioneered high-volume, affordable cardiac surgery in India.

events.title: Birth of Malaria Nobel Laureate Sir Ronald Ross in Almora
events.summary: Sir Ronald Ross was born in Almora in British India. Serving for 25 years in the Indian Medical Service, he proved in 1897 that mosquitoes transmit the malaria parasite, earning the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

events.title: WHO Declares India Free of Maternal and Neonatal Tetanus
events.summary: Following nationwide validation surveys across all 675 districts, the World Health Organization declared India to have achieved Maternal and Neonatal Tetanus Elimination (MNTE), reducing incidence to fewer than one case per 1,000 live births.
events.sourceTitle: Indian Journal of Communicable Diseases | Maternal and Neonatal Tetanus Elimination

events.title: Passing of Cardiologist and IMA Leader Dr. K. K. Aggarwal
events.summary: Padma Shri and Dr. B. C. Roy Awardee cardiologist Dr. Krishan Kumar Aggarwal passed away from COVID-19 in New Delhi. A former National President of the Indian Medical Association, he was widely known for public health education and CPR training.

events.title: Enactment of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA)
events.summary: India enacted the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003, prohibiting tobacco advertising and regulating the trade, supply, and distribution of tobacco products nationwide.
events.sourceTitle: Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act - Indian Kanoon

events.title: India's First Uterus Transplant Performed in Pune
events.summary: Dr. Shailesh Puntambekar and his surgical team at Galaxy Care Hospital in Pune performed India's first uterine transplant, transplanting a mother's womb into her daughter using laparoscopic retrieval.

events.title: Birth of Kala-azar Researcher Dr. Mohan Mishra
events.summary: Indian physician Dr. Mohan Mishra was born on this day. His clinical trials with Amphotericin B provided a breakthrough cure for drug-resistant visceral leishmaniasis (Kala-azar) in Bihar and eastern India.

events.title: India Receives WHO Certification for Trachoma Elimination
events.summary: India formally received the World Health Organization certification for eliminating trachoma as a public health problem, following decades of sustained eye health interventions under the SAFE strategy.
events.sourceTitle: India receives WHO certification for elimination of Trachoma as Public Health Problem - News On AIR

events.title: Passing of Cardiac Surgeon Dr. Nitu Mandke
events.summary: Pioneering Mumbai cardiac surgeon Dr. Nityanand Mandke passed away at age 55. Trained under Dr. P. K. Sen, he performed over 10,000 cardiac surgeries, mentored surgeons in off-pump techniques, and initiated the hospital project now known as Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital.

events.title: Birth of Cardiac Surgeon and Innovator Dr. M. S. Valiathan
events.summary: Dr. Marthanda Varma Sankaran Valiathan was born in Mavelikara, Travancore. A Padma Vibhushan cardiac surgeon and former Director of SCTIMST, he spearheaded the development of India's indigenous Chitra heart valve and promoted Ayurvedic biology.

events.title: Passing of CMC Vellore Founder Dr. Ida S. Scudder
events.summary: Medical missionary Dr. Ida Sophia Scudder passed away at age 89 in Kodaikanal. She founded the Christian Medical College & Hospital in Vellore in 1918 as a medical school for women, growing it into one of India's foremost medical institutions.

events.title: India Crosses 200 Million COVID-19 Vaccine Doses
events.summary: India surpassed 200 million cumulative COVID-19 vaccine doses administered nationwide during the expanded adult immunization campaign.

events.title: Passing of Pathologist & Nutrition Scientist Dr. Vulimiri Ramalingaswami
events.summary: Padma Vibhushan pathologist Dr. Vulimiri Ramalingaswami passed away at age 79. A former Director of AIIMS New Delhi and Director General of ICMR, his pioneering research on protein-energy malnutrition and iodine deficiency earned global acclaim.

events.title: Passing of Dr. T. M. A. Pai
events.summary: Dr. Tonse Madhava Ananth Pai, founder of Kasturba Medical College and architect of the Manipal university town, passed away in Manipal at age 81.

events.title: Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 Comes into Force
events.summary: India's Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 officially came into force nationwide, mandating parity between mental and physical health insurance and establishing Mental Health Review Boards.

events.title: First Classes Begin at Calcutta Medical College
events.summary: Academic classes commenced at Medical College & Hospital, Kolkata (Calcutta Medical College), marking the formal beginning of modern Western medical education in eastern India.

events.title: Data Collection Begins for National Mental Health Survey of India
events.summary: Field data collection began for the landmark National Mental Health Survey of India (2015–16) coordinated by NIMHANS, providing India's first comprehensive nationwide epidemiological baseline of mental disorders.
events.sourceTitle: National Mental Health Survey of India, 2015-16: Summary - NIMHANS

events.title: All-India Institute of Medical Sciences Act, 1956 Commences
events.summary: The All-India Institute of Medical Sciences Act, 1956 (Act 25 of 1956) was published and commenced, establishing AIIMS New Delhi as an autonomous institution of national importance for medical education, research, and tertiary care.
events.sourceTitle: All-India Institute of Medical Sciences Act, 1956 - Indian Kanoon

events.title: Passing of Obstetrician-Gynecologist Dr. Jerusha Jhirad
events.summary: Padma Shri physician Dr. Jerusha Jacob Jhirad passed away at age 93. She was the first Indian superintendent of Cama Hospital in Mumbai and conducted landmark statistical inquiries into maternal mortality.

events.title: Birth of Bio-organic Chemist Dr. Darshan Ranganathan
events.summary: Renowned Indian bio-organic chemist Dr. Darshan Ranganathan was born in Delhi; she later pioneered work in protein folding, self-assembling peptide nanotubes, and chemical simulation of the urea cycle.

events.title: Passing of Dr. Darshan Ranganathan
events.summary: Dr. Darshan Ranganathan passed away on her 60th birthday following a battle with breast cancer, leaving a prolific legacy in peptide chemistry and inspiring the biennial Professor Darshan Ranganathan Memorial Lecture.

events.title: Constitution of the Indian Red Cross Society
events.summary: Fifty members were formally nominated to constitute the Indian Red Cross Society under the Indian Red Cross Society Act (Act XV of 1920), establishing India's national humanitarian and disaster-relief health organization.
events.sourceTitle: About Us – Indian Red Cross Society

events.title: National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) Formed
events.summary: The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine officially came into existence, replacing the Central Council of Indian Medicine to regulate education and practice in Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, and Sowa-Rigpa.
events.sourceTitle: National Commission for Indian System of Medicine - Wikipedia

events.title: Passing of Sir Ram Nath Chopra, Father of Indian Pharmacology
events.summary: Colonel Sir Ram Nath Chopra passed away in Srinagar at age 90. Celebrated as the Father of Indian Pharmacology, he chaired the 1930–31 Drugs Enquiry Committee and pioneered research on indigenous medicinal plants such as Rauvolfia serpentina.

events.title: First Smallpox Vaccination Administered in India
events.summary: Three-year-old Anna Dusthall in Bombay (Mumbai) became the first person in India to receive the smallpox vaccine, initiating a chain of human-to-human lymph vaccination that spread to Madras, Poona, Hyderabad, and Surat.
events.sourceTitle: A brief history of vaccines & vaccination in India - PMC

events.title: Passing of IVF Pioneer Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay
events.summary: Physician and physiologist Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay passed away in Kolkata. In 1978, he had created India's first and the world's second test-tube baby, Kanupriya Agarwal (Durga), using cryopreserved embryos—an achievement formally recognized years after his death.

events.title: Birth of India's First Female Cardiologist Dr. S. I. Padmavati
events.summary: Padma Vibhushan awardee Dr. Sivaramakrishna Iyer Padmavati was born in 1917. She established India's first cardiac clinic and cardiac catheterization laboratory and founded the All India Heart Foundation.

events.title: Universal Free COVID-19 Vaccination Drive Begins with Record 8.6M Doses
events.summary: India commenced its universalized free COVID-19 vaccination drive for all adults, administering a then-record 8.6 million doses on the opening day.
events.sourceTitle: PIB's Bulletin on COVID-19 - Press Information Bureau

events.title: India Surpasses 300 Million COVID-19 Vaccine Doses
events.summary: India crossed the milestone of 300 million cumulative COVID-19 vaccine doses administered nationwide.

events.title: Passing of Dr. Ramchandra Dattatraya Lele, Father of Nuclear Medicine in India
events.summary: Padma Bhushan physician Dr. Ramchandra Dattatraya Lele passed away. Widely regarded as the Father of Nuclear Medicine in India, he pioneered clinical nuclear imaging and radioisotope therapeutics in the country.
events.sourceTitle: Salute to the Father of Nuclear Medicine in India - PMC

events.title: Founding of Kasturba Medical College (KMC), Manipal
events.summary: Dr. T. M. A. Pai established Kasturba Medical College in Manipal as India's first private, self-financing MBBS medical college, later expanding into Manipal Academy of Higher Education.

events.title: Birth of Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy
events.summary: Renowned Indian physician, medical educator, and statesman Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy was born in Bankipore, Patna. He later served as Chief Minister of West Bengal and was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1961.

events.title: Passing of Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy
events.summary: Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy passed away on his 80th birthday in Kolkata, prompting the institution of the Dr. B. C. Roy National Award in his memory the same year.

events.title: First National Doctors' Day Observed in India
events.summary: India officially observed its first National Doctors' Day on July 1 following a recommendation by the Indian Medical Association to honor Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy's birth and death anniversary.
events.sourceTitle: Monthly Current Affairs - July 2026 - SATHEE - IIT Kanpur

events.title: Ronald Ross Identifies Mosquito Salivary Glands as Malaria Storage Site
events.summary: Working in Calcutta on avian malaria, Ronald Ross discovered that the salivary glands of mosquitoes serve as the storage site for malaria parasites prior to transmission during biting.

events.title: Passing of Dr. Govindappa Venkataswamy
events.summary: Pioneering Indian ophthalmologist Dr. Govindappa Venkataswamy, founder of the Aravind Eye Hospital and Aurolab in Madurai, passed away at age 87. He personally performed over 100,000 eye surgeries and created a globally replicated high-volume, low-cost eye care model.

events.title: Transplantation of Human Organs Act, 1994 Enacted
events.summary: The Transplantation of Human Organs Act (Act 42 of 1994) received assent and was published in the Gazette of India, legally recognizing brain-stem death and regulating organ removal, storage, and transplantation while banning commercial organ trading.
events.sourceTitle: The Transplantation Of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994 - Indian Kanoon

events.title: WHO Felicitates India for Yaws-Free Status and Maternal & Neonatal Tetanus Elimination
events.summary: At a ceremony in New Delhi, the World Health Organization formally felicitated India for becoming the first country officially acknowledged as yaws-free and validated for Maternal and Neonatal Tetanus Elimination (MNTE).
events.sourceTitle: India's triumph over yaws adds momentum to global eradication - WHO

events.title: Launch of COVID Vaccination Amrit Mahotsav
events.summary: The Government of India launched a 75-day special mission-mode drive providing free COVID-19 precaution doses to all eligible adults at government vaccination centers nationwide.
events.sourceTitle: India achieves major landmark of '200 Crore' COVID-19 Vaccinations - PIB

events.title: Birth of Dr. Rustom Jal Vakil
events.summary: Pioneering Indian cardiologist Dr. Rustom Jal Vakil was born in Bombay. He introduced reserpine derived from Rauwolfia serpentina for treating hypertension and became the first Indian to win a Lasker Award.

events.title: India Surpasses 200 Crore COVID-19 Vaccine Doses
events.summary: India's nationwide COVID-19 immunization campaign crossed the milestone of 200 crore (2 billion) cumulative vaccine doses administered.
events.sourceTitle: India achieves major landmark of '200 Crore' COVID-19 Vaccinations - PIB

events.title: Passing of Dr. M. S. Valiathan
events.summary: Renowned Indian cardiac surgeon Dr. Marthanda Varma Sankaran Valiathan, former director of SCTIMST and pioneer behind the indigenous TTK Chitra heart valve, passed away in Manipal at age 90.

events.title: Birth of Dr. Kadambini Ganguly
events.summary: Dr. Kadambini Ganguly, one of India's first female university graduates and the first Indian woman to practice Western medicine in India, was born in Bhagalpur.

events.title: Passing of Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy
events.summary: Trailblazing Indian physician, legislator, and social reformer Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy, who founded the Adyar Cancer Institute in Chennai, passed away at age 81.

events.title: Passing of Dr. Prafulla Kumar Sen
events.summary: Pioneering Indian cardiothoracic surgeon Dr. P. K. Sen, who led India's first human heart transplant attempt at KEM Hospital in 1968 and pioneered open-heart and aortic surgery in India, passed away.

events.title: Birth of Dr. Chintaman Govind Pandit
events.summary: Indian virologist and medical administrator Dr. C. G. Pandit was born; he later served as the first Director of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR).

events.title: Passing of Dr. Obaid Siddiqi
events.summary: Pioneering Indian neurogeneticist and Founder-Director of the TIFR National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) in Bengaluru, Dr. Obaid Siddiqi, passed away.

events.title: Launch of National Viral Hepatitis Control Program
events.summary: Marking World Hepatitis Day, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched the National Viral Hepatitis Control Program in New Delhi to expand testing and treatment for hepatitis B and C and eliminate viral hepatitis by 2030.
events.sourceTitle: Shri J P Nadda Launches National Viral Hepatitis Control Program - PIB

events.title: Physician Dr. Mahendralal Sircar Founds IACS in Calcutta
events.summary: Renowned Calcutta physician Dr. Mahendralal Sircar founded the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), India's oldest autonomous scientific research institution.
events.sourceTitle: Indian Association For The Cultivation Of Science - Audiala

events.title: Birth of Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy
events.summary: Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy, one of India's first female doctors, first woman legislator in British India, and co-founder of Chennai's Cancer Institute (WIA), was born in Pudukkottai.

events.title: Malaria Institute of India Reorganized as NICD
events.summary: The Government of India renamed and expanded the Malaria Institute of India (MII) into the National Institute of Communicable Diseases (NICD) to cover broader infectious disease epidemiology and control.
events.sourceTitle: National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) - MoHFW

events.title: NICD Renamed National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)
events.summary: The National Institute of Communicable Diseases in New Delhi was officially renamed the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) with an expanded mandate for disease surveillance and outbreak response.
events.sourceTitle: National Centre for Disease Control - Wikipedia

events.title: Birth of Acharya Prafulla Chandra Ray
events.summary: Chemist and industrialist Sir Prafulla Chandra Ray, who founded Bengal Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals—India's first pharmaceutical company—was born in Bengal.

events.title: Birth of Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose
events.summary: Obstetrician and gynecologist Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose, India's first female Surgeon General and founder of the Nagercoil Tuberculosis Sanatorium, was born in Aymanam, Travancore.

events.title: India's First Successful Deceased-Donor Heart Transplant
events.summary: A 20-member surgical team led by Dr. P. Venugopal at AIIMS, New Delhi, performed India's first successful human-to-human heart transplant on 40-year-old recipient Devi Ram, who survived for 15 years post-surgery.
events.sourceTitle: How the longest survivors have lived for more than 33 years after a heart transplant - The Indian Express

events.title: Passing of Dr. Haimabati Sen
events.summary: Pioneering Indian woman physician Dr. Haimabati Sen, who practiced medicine in late 19th- and early 20th-century Bengal and authored a landmark memoir of colonial medical practice, passed away.

events.title: Birth of Harsha Chawda, India's First Scientifically Documented IVF Baby
events.summary: Dr. Indira Hinduja and Dr. Kusum Zaveri delivered Harsha Chawda at KEM Hospital in Mumbai, marking India's first scientifically documented in vitro fertilization (IVF) birth.
events.sourceTitle: Mumbai's first IVF baby delivers her baby - The Indian Express

events.title: Birth of Dr. M. S. Swaminathan
events.summary: Indian geneticist and agricultural scientist Dr. Mankombu Sambasivan Swaminathan, whose Green Revolution work transformed India's food security and nutritional landscape, was born in Kumbakonam.
events.sourceTitle: M. S. Swaminathan - Simple English Wikipedia

events.title: G. N. Ramachandran Publishes Triple-Helical Structure of Collagen
events.summary: Biophysicist G. N. Ramachandran and Gopinath Kartha published their landmark Nature paper from Madras proposing the triple-helical 'Madras' model of collagen, the most abundant protein in the human body.
events.sourceTitle: GNR Cracked the Structure of Collagen - The Better India

events.title: Birth of Dr. Vulimiri Ramalingaswami
events.summary: Renowned Indian pathologist and nutrition researcher Dr. V. Ramalingaswami, who served as Director of AIIMS New Delhi and Director General of ICMR, was born in Srikakulam.

events.title: Passing of Dr. Yellapragada Subbarow
events.summary: Indian-born biochemist Dr. Yellapragada Subbarow, who discovered ATP's role in cellular energy, synthesized folic acid and methotrexate, and developed diethylcarbamazine (DEC) for filariasis, passed away in New York.

events.title: Presidential Assent to the National Medical Commission Act, 2019
events.summary: The National Medical Commission Act, 2019 received Presidential assent, establishing the statutory framework to replace the Medical Council of India and reform medical education regulation in India.

events.title: Establishment of Plague Research Laboratory (Haffkine Institute)
events.summary: Dr. Waldemar Haffkine established the Plague Research Laboratory in Parel, Bombay—later renamed the Haffkine Institute—after developing the world's first human plague vaccine in India.

events.title: Parliament Passes Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act
events.summary: The Parliament of India passed the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971, legalizing safe abortion under specified medical and humanitarian conditions up to 20 weeks of gestation.
events.sourceTitle: Abortion Laws in India - Naya Legal

events.title: Birth of Dr. Prakash Narain Tandon
events.summary: Eminent Indian neurosurgeon and neuroscientist Dr. P. N. Tandon, who founded the Department of Neurosurgery at AIIMS New Delhi and helped establish the National Brain Research Centre (NBRC), was born in Shimla.

events.title: Launch of National Digital Health Mission (NDHM)
events.summary: On India's 74th Independence Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the National Digital Health Mission to create unique digital health IDs and an interoperable national health data ecosystem.
events.sourceTitle: National Digital Health Mission - Vajiram & Ravi

events.title: Mental Health Care Bill Introduced in Rajya Sabha
events.summary: The Mental Health Care Bill, 2013 was introduced in the Rajya Sabha, initiating landmark legislative reform that culminated in the rights-based Mental Healthcare Act, 2017.

events.title: Ronald Ross Discovers Malaria Parasite in Anopheles Mosquito in Secunderabad
events.summary: Working at Begumpet Military Hospital in Secunderabad, Sir Ronald Ross identified Plasmodium malaria parasites in the stomach wall of an Anopheles mosquito, proving mosquito-borne transmission and inspiring World Mosquito Day.

events.title: DCGI Approves ZyCoV-D, World's First Plasmid DNA COVID-19 Vaccine
events.summary: The Drugs Controller General of India granted Emergency Use Authorization to Zydus Cadila's ZyCoV-D, the world's first needle-free, plasmid DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine.
events.sourceTitle: World's First Plasmid-based DNA COVID-19 Vaccine Received EUA in India - DCVMN

events.title: Passing of Dr. S. I. Padmavati, India's First Female Cardiologist
events.summary: Dr. Sivaramakrishna Iyer Padmavati, India's first woman cardiologist and founder of the All India Heart Foundation and National Heart Institute in Delhi, passed away at age 103 from COVID-19.

events.title: Launch of National Nutrition Week in India
events.summary: The Food and Nutrition Board initiated India's annual National Nutrition Week (September 1–7) to raise public awareness about balanced diets, micronutrients, and combating malnutrition.

events.title: Birth of Dr. K. K. Aggarwal
events.summary: Cardiologist, Padma Shri awardee, and former National President of the Indian Medical Association Dr. Krishan Kumar Aggarwal was born in New Delhi.

events.title: DCGI Approves Bharat Biotech's iNCOVACC Intranasal COVID-19 Vaccine
events.summary: The Drugs Controller General of India approved Bharat Biotech's iNCOVACC (BBV154) for restricted emergency use in adults, making it the world's first intranasal COVID-19 vaccine to receive regulatory approval.
events.sourceTitle: Bharat Biotech's intranasal Covid vaccine gets DCGI nod - The Indian Express

events.title: Passing of Dr. Chintaman Govind Pandit
events.summary: Dr. C. G. Pandit, founding Director of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and Padma Bhushan awardee, passed away at age 96.

events.title: Launch of Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
events.summary: President Droupadi Murmu virtually launched the Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan to mobilize community and corporate nutritional support (Ni-kshay Mitra) toward India's tuberculosis elimination goals.
events.sourceTitle: President of India launches Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan - PIB

events.title: India's Second Human Heart Transplant Performed by Dr. P. K. Sen
events.summary: Cardiothoracic surgeon Dr. P. K. Sen performed India's second human heart transplant at KEM Hospital in Bombay, though the recipient succumbed to pulmonary hypertension 14 hours post-operatively.

events.title: Launch of Ayushman Bhav Campaign
events.summary: President Droupadi Murmu virtually launched the nationwide Ayushman Bhav campaign from Gandhinagar to achieve saturation coverage of Ayushman cards, ABHA IDs, and community health screenings.
events.sourceTitle: President of India virtually launches Ayushman Bhav Campaign - PIB

events.title: India Sets Single-Day Record of 2.5 Crore COVID-19 Vaccine Doses
events.summary: India's national COVID-19 immunization program achieved its highest single-day vaccination total, administering 2.5 crore doses in 24 hours.
events.sourceTitle: India achieves major landmark of '200 Crore' COVID-19 Vaccinations - PIB

events.title: Inauguration of Apollo Hospitals in Chennai
events.summary: Founded by cardiologist Dr. Prathap C. Reddy, Apollo Hospitals opened in Chennai as India's first corporate hospital, ushering in private tertiary and quaternary healthcare infrastructure across the country.

events.title: Birth of Dr. Asima Chatterjee
events.summary: Organic chemist and phytomedicine pioneer Dr. Asima Chatterjee was born in Calcutta; she became the first woman to earn a D.Sc. from an Indian university and developed the anti-epileptic drug Ayush-56 alongside research on vinca alkaloids and anti-malarials.

events.title: Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose Takes Oath as India's First Woman Legislator
events.summary: Physician and Acting Surgeon General of Travancore Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose took oath as a member of the Travancore Legislative Council, becoming India's first female legislator while championing public health reforms.
events.sourceTitle: Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose: India's first female legislator - The Hindu

events.title: Launch of Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)
events.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched AB-PMJAY in Ranchi, Jharkhand, establishing one of the world's largest government-funded health assurance schemes for secondary and tertiary hospitalization.
events.sourceTitle: Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Aarogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) - PIB

events.title: Birth of Dr. Autar Singh Paintal
events.summary: Indian physiologist Dr. Autar Singh Paintal was born in Mogok; he discovered pulmonary J-receptors and became the first Indian physiologist elected Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS), later serving as DG of ICMR.

events.title: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021 Enforced
events.summary: Notified in the Gazette of India, the MTP Amendment Act, 2021 came into force, extending the upper gestation limit for abortion to 24 weeks for special categories and expanding access to unmarried women.

events.title: Passing of Dr. Rukhmabai
events.summary: Dr. Rukhmabai, colonial India's second qualified and practicing woman physician and a landmark figure in social reform leading to the Age of Consent Act, passed away in Bombay at age 90.

events.title: National Medical Commission (NMC) Replaces Medical Council of India
events.summary: The National Medical Commission formally came into force, repealing the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 and dissolving the Medical Council of India as the apex regulator of medical education and practice.

events.title: National Rollout of Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)
events.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the nationwide rollout of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission via video conference to build India's interoperable digital health infrastructure and ABHA health accounts.
events.sourceTitle: PM launches Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission - PIB

events.title: Passing of Dr. M. S. Swaminathan
events.summary: Geneticist and architect of India's Green Revolution Dr. M. S. Swaminathan, whose work eradicated chronic famine and reshaped nutritional security in India, passed away at age 98.
events.sourceTitle: M. S. Swaminathan - Simple English Wikipedia

events.title: Supreme Court Affirms Equal Abortion Rights Regardless of Marital Status
events.summary: In X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Govt. of NCT of Delhi, a three-judge bench of the Supreme Court of India ruled that all women, married or unmarried, have the right to safe and legal abortion up to 24 weeks.
events.sourceTitle: X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department - Wikipedia

events.title: Madras Medical School Elevated to Madras Medical College
events.summary: The Madras Medical School was formally accorded college status as Madras Medical College, becoming one of India's earliest premier institutions for modern medical education. Its first batch of diplomates graduated in 1852.

events.title: First National Voluntary Blood Donation Day Observed in India
events.summary: The Indian Society of Blood Transfusion and Immunohaematology initiated the first National Voluntary Blood Donation Day across India to promote safe, non-remunerated blood donation.

events.title: Launch of Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)
events.summary: The Government of India launched the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme to combat malnutrition, reduce infant and maternal mortality, and deliver supplementary nutrition and health check-ups through Anganwadi centres.
events.sourceTitle: Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) - NIC Kargil

events.title: Death of Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose, India's First Female Surgeon General
events.summary: Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose, pioneering gynaecologist, founder of the Tuberculosis Sanatorium in Nagercoil, and the first woman appointed Surgeon General in India (Travancore, 1938), passed away at age 90.

events.title: Launch of the Pulse Polio Immunisation Programme in Delhi
events.summary: India rolled out its first Pulse Polio Immunisation drive in Delhi, administering oral polio drops across 4,000 booths and laying the foundation for the nationwide campaign that eventually eradicated wild poliovirus from India.
events.sourceTitle: Photo of the day: Queue for life - Forbes India

events.title: Death of Dr. Kadambini Ganguly, India's First Practicing Female Physician
events.summary: Dr. Kadambini Ganguly, one of India's first two female doctors of Western medicine and the first woman admitted to Calcutta Medical College (1883), passed away in Calcutta after performing a surgical operation the same day.

events.title: Birth of Kanupriya Agarwal (Durga), India's First IVF Baby
events.summary: Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay and colleagues achieved the birth of Kanupriya Agarwal ('Durga') in Kolkata via in-vitro fertilisation, making her India's first and the world's second test-tube baby.

events.title: Birth of Dr. G. N. Ramachandran, Structural Biology Pioneer
events.summary: Born in Ernakulam, Dr. G. N. Ramachandran revolutionized molecular biophysics by proposing the triple-helical structure of collagen and creating the Ramachandran plot for analyzing peptide conformations.

events.title: Death of Dr. Dilip Mahalanabis, Pioneer of Oral Rehydration Therapy
events.summary: Indian paediatrician Dr. Dilip Mahalanabis, whose field deployment of Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) during the 1971 refugee crisis saved millions of lives worldwide from cholera and diarrheal dehydration, died in Kolkata.

events.title: Dedication of the All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA) in New Delhi
events.summary: On the second National Ayurveda Day, the All India Institute of Ayurveda in New Delhi was dedicated to the nation as an apex autonomous institute for postgraduate education, research, and integrative clinical care.

events.title: Founding of the Calcutta School of Medicine (Now R. G. Kar Medical College)
events.summary: Dr. Radha Gobinda Kar and fellow Indian physicians founded the Calcutta School of Medicine, establishing Asia's first private medical college to advance self-sufficiency in medical education.

events.title: India Surpasses 1 Billion (100 Crore) COVID-19 Vaccine Doses
events.summary: India's nationwide COVID-19 immunization campaign crossed the landmark milestone of 100 crore (one billion) cumulative vaccine doses administered.
events.sourceTitle: India achieves the major milestone of 'one billion' vaccinations - PIB

events.title: Death of Waldemar Haffkine, Developer of India's Plague Vaccine
events.summary: Bacteriologist Waldemar Haffkine, who conducted cholera vaccine trials in India in 1893 and developed the bubonic plague vaccine at Grant Medical College, Bombay in 1897 (founding what became the Haffkine Institute), died in Lausanne.

events.title: First National Ayurveda Day Observed in India
events.summary: The Ministry of AYUSH inaugurated India's first National Ayurveda Day, launching 'Mission Madhumeha through Ayurveda' and releasing national protocols for diabetes prevention and control.
events.sourceTitle: First Ever National Day of Ayurveda being celebrated throughout the Country - PIB

events.title: Birth of Dr. Khwaja Abdul Hamied, Founder of Cipla
events.summary: Born in Aligarh, industrial and pharmaceutical chemist Dr. Khwaja Abdul Hamied founded Cipla in 1935, laying a cornerstone for indigenous pharmaceutical manufacturing and affordable generic medicines in India.
events.sourceTitle: Khwaja Abdul Hamied - Simple English Wikipedia

events.title: First Batch of Students Admitted to Grant Medical College, Bombay
events.summary: Grant Medical College in Bombay (now Mumbai) admitted its inaugural cohort of medical students, marking the formal beginning of one of India's oldest and most influential medical institutions.
events.sourceTitle: Grant Medical College and Sir J. J. Group of Hospitals - Wikipedia

events.title: Birth of Dr. Gagandeep Kang, Virologist and Rotavac Investigator
events.summary: Born in Shimla, CMC Vellore physician-scientist Dr. Gagandeep Kang played a pivotal role in developing India's indigenous rotavirus vaccine (Rotavac) and became the first Indian woman elected Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS).

events.title: WHO Grants Emergency Use Listing (EUL) to Covaxin
events.summary: The World Health Organization granted Emergency Use Listing to Hyderabad-based Bharat Biotech's indigenous COVID-19 vaccine Covaxin, clearing it for global distribution through COVAX.
events.sourceTitle: WHO green-lights India's COVID vaccine as global cases rise - CIDRAP

events.title: India's First Deceased-Donor Liver Transplant Performed in New Delhi
events.summary: Surgeons Dr. A. S. Soin and Dr. Rajashekar performed India's first deceased-donor liver transplant at Apollo Hospital, New Delhi, on a 42-year-old recipient.
events.sourceTitle: First Organ and Tissue Transplants - Donate Life

events.title: First National Cancer Awareness Day Observed in India
events.summary: Established by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare on Marie Curie's birth anniversary, India observed its first National Cancer Awareness Day to promote cancer prevention, screening, and early detection.
events.sourceTitle: National Cancer Awareness Day in India - PIB

events.title: Birth of Dr. Maharaj Kishan Bhan, Co-Developer of Rotavac
events.summary: Born in Srinagar, pediatrician and clinical scientist Dr. M. K. Bhan led landmark research on diarrheal diseases, collaborated on developing the indigenous Rotavac vaccine, and founded BIRAC as DBT Secretary.

events.title: Death of Dr. Har Gobind Khorana, 1968 Nobel Laureate in Medicine
events.summary: Indian-born biochemist Dr. Har Gobind Khorana, who won the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for elucidating the genetic code and its role in protein synthesis, died in Concord, Massachusetts.

events.title: Birth of Dr. Dilip Mahalanabis, Oral Rehydration Therapy Trailblazer
events.summary: Born in Kishoreganj (Bengal Province), Calcutta Medical College alumnus Dr. Dilip Mahalanabis pioneered the large-scale clinical use of oral rehydration therapy (ORT) to dramatically cut cholera mortality.
events.sourceTitle: Dr. Dilip Mahalanabis (1934-2022): Trailblazer in Diarrheal Disease - PMC

events.title: NIMHANS Conferred Deemed University Status
events.summary: The University Grants Commission declared the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru, a Deemed University with academic autonomy.
events.sourceTitle: NIMHANS to be declared institute of national importance - The Hindu

events.title: Establishment of the Indian Research Fund Association (Now ICMR)
events.summary: Sir Harcourt Butler established the Indian Research Fund Association (IRFA) to sponsor and coordinate medical research across India; it was redesignated as the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) in 1949.
events.sourceTitle: History | Indian Council of Medical Research

events.title: India's First Successful Living-Donor Pediatric Liver Transplant
events.summary: At Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals in New Delhi, 20-month-old Sanjay Kandasamy received a segment of his father's liver in India's first successful pediatric liver transplant; he later grew up to become a medical doctor.

events.title: Launch of India's Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)
events.summary: The Government of India launched the Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) to provide universal, free vaccination against major vaccine-preventable diseases for infants and pregnant women across all districts.
events.sourceTitle: BCG immunization coverage estimates of India and Brazil - ResearchGate

events.title: Death of Dr. S. S. Badrinath, Founder of Sankara Nethralaya
events.summary: Renowned vitreoretinal surgeon and Padma Bhushan awardee Dr. Sengamedu Srinivasa Badrinath, who founded the charitable eye hospital Sankara Nethralaya in Chennai in 1978, passed away at age 83.

events.title: Birth of Dr. Rukhmabai, Pioneer Female Physician and Social Reformer
events.summary: Born in Bombay, Dr. Rukhmabai qualified in medicine in Edinburgh in 1894 to become one of colonial India's first practicing women doctors, serving for decades as Chief Medical Officer at women's hospitals in Surat and Rajkot.

events.title: Serum Institute of India Passes 1 Billion COVISHIELD Dose Milestone
events.summary: Pune-based Serum Institute of India announced it had produced 1 billion doses of the COVISHIELD COVID-19 vaccine and resumed global exports to low- and middle-income countries via COVAX.
events.sourceTitle: Serum Institute Of India Press Release - 26 November 2021

events.title: Birth of Dr. Pramod Karan Sethi, Co-Inventor of the Jaipur Foot
events.summary: Born in Varanasi, orthopaedic surgeon Dr. P. K. Sethi co-developed the low-cost, flexible Jaipur Foot prosthesis in 1969 with craftsman Ram Chandra Sharma, transforming amputee rehabilitation worldwide.
events.sourceTitle: Legends of Indian Orthopedics: Pramod Karan Sethi - PMC

events.title: Incorporation of Biocon India in Bengaluru
events.summary: Biocon India Private Limited was incorporated in Bengaluru, evolving from an enzyme manufacturer into one of India's leading biopharmaceutical enterprises producing biosimilars and human insulin.

events.title: Bhopal Methyl Isocyanate Gas Disaster
events.summary: Over 40 tons of toxic methyl isocyanate gas leaked from the Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, exposing more than half a million people and becoming one of the worst toxicological and public health catastrophes in history.
events.sourceTitle: The Bhopal disaster and its aftermath: a review - PMC

events.title: Birth of Dr. Ida Sophia Scudder, Founder of CMC Vellore
events.summary: Born in Ranipet, India, Dr. Ida Scudder dedicated her life to women's healthcare and medical education in India, founding the Christian Medical College and Hospital in Vellore in 1918.

events.title: First Nationwide National Immunization Day (Pulse Polio) in India
events.summary: The Government of India conducted its first nationwide National Immunization Day for poliomyelitis eradication, vaccinating approximately 87 million children under three years of age.
events.sourceTitle: A brief history of vaccines & vaccination in India - PMC

events.title: Sir Ronald Ross Receives the Nobel Prize for Malaria Discovery in India
events.summary: Indian Medical Service officer Ronald Ross received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in Stockholm for demonstrating that Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria, a breakthrough achieved during his work in Secunderabad and Calcutta.
events.sourceTitle: Physiology or Medicine 1902 - Award ceremony speech - NobelPrize.org

events.title: Har Gobind Khorana Receives the Nobel Prize for Deciphering the Genetic Code
events.summary: Indian-born biochemist Har Gobind Khorana received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in Stockholm alongside Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg for interpreting the genetic code and its function in protein synthesis.
events.sourceTitle: Award ceremony speech - Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1968 - NobelPrize.org

events.title: Death of Dr. B. Ramamurthi, 'Father of Neurosurgery in India'
events.summary: Dr. Balasubramaniam Ramamurthi, who established India's first dedicated neurosurgery department at Madras Medical College in 1950 and helped establish the National Brain Research Centre, passed away.

events.title: Birth of Sir Upendranath Brahmachari, Discoverer of Urea Stibamine
events.summary: Born in Sardanga, West Bengal, physician and scientist Sir Upendranath Brahmachari synthesized urea stibamine in 1922, providing the first effective cure for kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) and saving millions of lives.
events.sourceTitle: Dr. Upendranath Brahmachari: The Unsung Hero of Indian Medical Science - PMC

events.title: Death of Dr. Autar Singh Paintal, Discoverer of J-Receptors
events.summary: Dr. Autar Singh Paintal, the first Indian physiologist elected Fellow of the Royal Society and former Director General of ICMR who discovered pulmonary J-receptors and atrial B receptors, died in New Delhi.

events.title: Launch of Mission Indradhanush Immunization Drive
events.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched Mission Indradhanush as a targeted catch-up vaccination campaign under the Universal Immunization Programme to achieve at least 90% full immunization coverage among children and pregnant women.

events.title: Birth of Dr. Sushila Nayyar, Union Health Minister and Founder of MGIMS
events.summary: Born in Kunjah, Punjab, Lady Hardinge Medical College alumna Dr. Sushila Nayyar served as Mahatma Gandhi's personal physician, twice as India's Health Minister, and founded the Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (MGIMS) in Sevagram in 1969.

events.title: Formation of NIMHANS in Bengaluru
events.summary: The All India Institute of Mental Health (est. 1954) and the Mysore State Mental Hospital were amalgamated to form the autonomous National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS) in Bengaluru.
events.sourceTitle: NIMHANS to be declared institute of national importance - The Hindu

events.title: Founding of the Indian Medical Association (IMA)
events.summary: At the 5th All India Medical Conference in Calcutta under the presidency of Dr. G. V. Deshmukh, Indian doctors passed a resolution establishing the All India Medical Association, renamed the Indian Medical Association in 1930.

events.title: DCGI Approves Indigenous COVID-19 Vaccine Corbevax
events.summary: The Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) granted restricted emergency use approval for Biological E's protein subunit COVID-19 vaccine Corbevax among adults.
events.sourceTitle: DBT-BIRAC supported Novel COVID-19 vaccine candidate - PIB

events.title: Inauguration of the All India Institute of Hygiene and Public Health (AIIH&PH)
events.summary: Established in Kolkata with assistance from the Rockefeller Foundation, the All India Institute of Hygiene and Public Health was inaugurated as India's pioneering institution for public health research and training.
events.sourceTitle: All India Institute of Hygiene and Public Health - Wikipedia
